source.title: Order and Chaos: NTK views on DNN Normalization, Checkerboard and Boundary Artifacts
source.authors: Arthur Jacot; Franck Gabriel; F. Ged; Clément Hongler

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some PDF extraction artifacts and corrupted characters appear, but the relevant sections are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analytically studies how normalization affects the infinite-width NTK and reports numerical GAN outcomes for normalization choices. These bear on V6's normalization-related training effects, but it does not measure the accuracy-learning-speed or learning-rate-tolerance outcomes named in V6.
record.gate_note: Most results concern NTK kernels, checkerboard and border artifacts, and GAN sample quality rather than the training classification-error outcomes in V1–V4 or the learning-rate dynamics in V5. V6 is tested only insofar as the paper compares normalization choices and reports GAN training outcomes; no accuracy-versus-training-time or learning-rate-tolerance comparison is reported. Cited prior findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports NTK structure, theoretical implications for optimization, and qualitative GAN samples. These do not measure the training error, initialization-dependent learning speed or depth, stability-threshold dynamics, or batch-normalization accuracy gains and learning-rate tolerance named by V1–V6. Comparing normalization choices alone does not test V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that ordered-regime NTKs favor constant and checkerboard modes, slowing training and potentially contributing to GAN collapse. They present nonlinearity normalization, parent-based parametrization, and layer-dependent learning rates as remedies, supported by theory and qualitative GAN illustrations, including samples without batch normalization.
record.recipe_differences: Infinite-width NTK analysis and DCGAN experiments focused on kernel structure and generated-image artifacts, rather than the classification-training recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Normalization choice and nonlinearity choice change the NTK regime and the reported GAN outcome; the paper also says parent-based parametrization and layer-dependent learning rates affect artifacts.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 3–4 show that normalized infinite-width NTKs approach a constant in the ordered regime and a Kronecker delta in the chaotic regime. The authors infer slower training from the constant component.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth and the activation/bias-dependent order–chaos regime determine infinite-width NTK structure and its implied optimization behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Propositions 5–6 connect post-activation layer normalization to normalized nonlinearities and chaos. Lemma 7 shows that post-activation batch normalization after the last hidden layer controls the NTK's constant component. These are kernel results, without measured accuracy-learning speed or learning-rate tolerance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization placement and type alter the constant component and order–chaos behavior of the studied NTKs.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4.1 and the authors' discussion report checkerboard collapse for the ordered ReLU GAN and its avoidance with normalized ReLU or batch normalization. Qualitative CelebA samples also demonstrate successful generation without batch normalization using other architectural and training choices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the illustrated DCGAN setting, normalization and other tuning choices can prevent checkerboard collapse and produce good samples without batch normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: The parent-based parametrization removes position-dependent border effects in the analyzed kernels; layer-dependent learning rates rebalance layer contributions and reduce checkerboard artifacts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parent-based parametrization and layer-dependent learning rates control border and checkerboard artifacts in deconvolutional networks.

record.problems: GAN outcomes are presented as images without quantified sample-quality measures or uncertainty. The text does not give classification training-error measurements, accuracy-learning curves, or learning-rate tolerance comparisons for the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible rows: the paper's numerical results are shown as GAN images and kernel visualizations, without a reported numerical outcome for a measure named by the tested version. Theoretical NTK results are not training-error measurements.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random labels and the effects of size, early stopping, and regularization.
Spurious local minima and the benefit of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training error in plain versus residual networks, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons measuring learning speed or trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Loss, curvature, sharpness, recovery, and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Accuracy gained over training time and tolerance of higher learning rates with versus without batch normalization; Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's V6 tested status to not tested. No eligible result rows or verdicts are required: the kernel proxies and GAN artifact outcomes address related constructs outside the supplied versions.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network training error as depth grows; training of very deep plain or unnormalized residual networks.
Initialization comparisons for training speed or trainable depth, including very deep tanh and convolutional networks.
Training dynamics above or near a learning-rate stability threshold, including loss, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.

The paper analytically compares normalization's effect on NTK structure and reports GAN outcomes, but does not report accuracy gained over training time or tolerance to higher learning rates as V6 states.
